subject: Request: one-time top-up credit due to product timing / SLA gap

Subject: Production timeline gap — credit request

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Satori is very eager to move forward, but the team flagged a couple of items that will materially affect our rollout timeline:

- The per-request SLA metrics we discussed (tail-latency SLA and per-tenant isolation) won’t be available until Redwood Private v1.2, which your product team confirmed ships in late September.
- We have a customer pilot that needs the higher isolation guarantees the week of Sep 20; without them, our pilot slides into Q4 and changes the go-live economics.

Given the timing mismatch, procurement has asked whether Redwood can provide a one-time top-up credit to cover the incremental hosting and support costs through the delay (they've modeled ~$42k). This is an ask to keep the initial contract value intact and avoid slipping the pilot.

I attached a short SLO deck we shared internally. Can you let us know what exceptions are possible and what approvals are required? We can also route a formal credit memo if that helps.

Appreciate any guidance — happy to jump on a call today.

Best,
Megan Li

Satori Analytics

Hi team,

Quick product clarifications and options:

Timeline: Private v1.2 (includes tenant-level KV isolation and the tail-latency mitigations referenced) is on track for the 28 Sep 2026 release window. We do not have a reliable path to fully ship before Sep 20 without impacting other customers.

Workarounds we can offer immediately (short-term):
- Apply a per-tenant request cap + dedicated small pool (software isolation) for the pilot — reduces risk but doesn't meet our formal SLA.
- Increase monitoring + a named support rotation during pilot weeks.

Commercial proposal (to balance customer retention and precedent):
- Offer a one-time top-up credit of $30,000 to offset the pilot cost if Satori signs the initial annual contract by Aug 25 and agrees to a public case study after the pilot completes.
- Alternatively, if they need the full $42k, require CSM-managed rollback terms and a revenue-protection clause (credits recovered pro rata over first two invoices if they churn within 90 days).

I'll attach a short note with the timeline and proposed mitigations for legal/finance review. From a product perspective, the $30k one-time credit aligns with our expected delta and keeps precedent manageable.

Aditya
